cards.text: Saul, king of Israel, is dead, and David has been anointed king over Judah at Hebron (1 Samuel 31:6; 2 Samuel 2:4). Now ALL the tribes of Israel come to David there. That's a CROWD, friend, and the biggest one I ever got in that junk drawer was one scared can opener sliding in.

cards.question: The tribes of Israel have come to David at Hebron. How do they describe themselves to him?

cards.text: Then they bring up the old days, back while Saul was still king over them.

cards.question: Even while Saul was king over them, the tribes say it was ___ who led Israel out and brought them back.

cards.text: And they remind David what the LORD said to him: "You will shepherd My people Israel, and you will be ruler over them." Friend, you don't forget a word like that.
So the elders of Israel come to King David at Hebron, and he makes a covenant with them before the LORD. Not a handshake, not a thumbs-up in the group chat, a COVENANT!

cards.question: After King David makes a covenant with the elders of Israel at Hebron, what do the elders do?

answers.text: Make him commander of the army
Bring him the crown of Saul

cards.question: David is thirty years old when he becomes king.

cards.text: And David reigns FORTY years, starting with seven years and six months over Judah in Hebron. Friend, I couldn't keep one stamp sharp for forty years!

cards.question: After Hebron, David reigns thirty-three years over all Israel and Judah. From which city?

cards.text: One little problem: Jerusalem isn't David's yet. When David and his men march against the Jebusites who live there, the Jebusites have something to say.

cards.question: David and his men march on Jerusalem. What do the Jebusites tell David?

answers.text: Even the blind and lame can repel you
Pay us and we will open the gates
Our king will come out to meet you

cards.text: They're SO sure, they even think it to themselves: "David cannot get in here." Friend, I said that about my chocolate chip bin once. Famous last words.

cards.question: Nevertheless, David captures the fortress of ___, also known as the City of ___.

cards.text: On that day, David gives the plan for reaching the lame and blind who are despised by David.

cards.question: What does David say whoever attacks the Jebusites must use?

cards.text: That's why people say, "The blind and the lame will never enter the palace." Then David moves into the fortress and calls it the City of David.

cards.question: Once he moves in, David builds up the City of David all the way around, from the supporting terraces inward.
From there, David becomes greater and greater. What's behind it all?

answers.text: The LORD God of Hosts was with him
Saul's family made peace with him

cards.text: Hiram, king of Tyre, sends envoys to David with cedar logs, carpenters and stonemasons. That's not a housewarming gift, friend, that's a WHOLE construction crew!

cards.question: Hiram's carpenters and stonemasons build a ___ for David.
David realizes the LORD has established him as king and exalted his kingdom for David's own sake.

cards.text: After arriving from Hebron, David takes more concubines and wives from Jerusalem, and more sons and daughters are born to him. The passage names eleven children born to him in Jerusalem, and two of those names are Nathan and Solomon.

findings.problem: Stop 2's choice cards open with the same type sequence as all of Stop 1: multiple choice, fill in the blank, multiple choice, true or false, multiple choice (Stop 2 cards 2, 4, 6, 8, 9 match Stop 1 cards 2, 4, 7, 8, 10). The types follow a repeated pattern instead of being chosen naturally for each card.

rule.text: No formula. Which question type comes next, the order the types come in and where a blank falls are chosen naturally for each card. They never follow a pattern. No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.

findings.problem: The wrong answer 'Strangers from far away' isn't believable. The speakers are the tribes of Israel, who were already ruled by Saul, so no baker would think they call themselves strangers from far away.

rule.text: Wrong answers for what someone does or says only need to be believable.

findings.problem: The right answer 'The LORD God of Hosts was with him' uses the Bible's wording and sounds like Scripture. The wrong answers ('The Jebusites joined his army', 'Saul's family made peace with him') are plain modern phrasing, so the right answer stands out.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: The joke 'That's not a housewarming gift' tells the baker that a house for David is being built. That points straight to 'palace' on card 11 and rules out the wrong answers 'temple' and 'tower'.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The last card of the passage, which also ends the whole story group, is a flat list summary with none of Papa Dorin's voice. 'The passage names eleven children' reads like a study note, not like Papa Dorin telling the moment.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.
